name: Hurro-Hittite Song of Emergence (formerly Song of Kumarbi)
language: Hittite adaptation of an earlier, probably Hurrian composition
source_label: Song of Emergence / former Song of Kumarbi

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: The narrative survives in Hittite cuneiform material from the Late Bronze Age Hittite imperial archive. This broad range avoids assigning a false exact tablet date.

earliest_written_attestation.note: The surviving Hittite adaptation belongs to the second millennium BCE; scholarship treats it as adapting an earlier, now-lost and probably Hurrian composition.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: Hittite-language cuneiform witnesses preserve the narrative; the exact date of each fragment is not collapsed into a single year here.

tradition_internal_claim.note: The narrative concerns primordial divine kingship and does not give a historical calendar date.

dating.dating_summary: The Song survives in a Late Bronze Age Hittite adaptation of an earlier, probably Hurrian composition; the surviving textual horizon is much firmer than the date or form of any earlier oral version.

notes: Added for Phase 7 transmission analysis. Similarity to Hesiod is not itself treated as influence; the separate relationship claim carries the transmission argument and its evidentiary limits.
